stem: Prove: A quadrilateral with four equal angles is a rectangle
stem_lead: Prove: A quadrilateral with four equal angles is a rectangle

mark_scheme.text: Assume that the four interior angles of quadrilateral ABCD are equal, then ∠A=∠B=∠C=∠D. And because the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral is 360°, so 4∠A=360°, we get ∠A=90°, so all four angles are 90°. Therefore AB⊥BC, BC⊥CD, CD⊥DA, DA⊥AB. From AB⊥BC and CD⊥BC, we can get AB∥CD; from BC⊥AB and AD⊥AB, we can get BC∥AD. Therefore, ABCD is a parallelogram and one of its angles is a right angle, so ABCD is a rectangle.

examiner_comment.text: Using the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral as 360°, first find out that each angle is 90°; then use "two straight lines perpendicular to a straight line are parallel to each other" to deduce that two sets of opposite sides are parallel, and obtain a parallelogram; finally use "a parallelogram with one right angle is a rectangle" to complete the proof.

examiner_comment.text: Let the two long sides of the board be a and b, and a∥b. Saw twice along the direction perpendicular to the long side to obtain two sections c and d, and c⊥a, d⊥a, so c∥d. The cut pedal has a and b as one set of opposite sides, c and d as another set of opposite sides, and the two sets of opposite sides are parallel respectively; there is also c⊥a, so the quadrilateral has a right angle and the opposite sides are parallel, which is equivalent to a rectangle.

We call the quadrilateral formed by connecting the midpoints of each side of any quadrilateral in sequence called a midpoint quadrilateral.

(1) What is the shape of the midpoint quadrilateral of any quadrilateral? Why?  
(2) What is the shape of the midpoint quadrilateral of any parallelogram? Why?  
(3) What are the shapes of the midpoint quadrilaterals of any rectangle, rhombus and square? Why?
stem_lead:
We call the quadrilateral formed by connecting the midpoints of each side of any quadrilateral in sequence called a midpoint quadrilateral.

(1) What is the shape of the midpoint quadrilateral of any quadrilateral? Why?  
(2) What is the shape of the midpoint quadrilateral of any parallelogram? Why?  
(3) What are the shapes of the midpoint quadrilaterals of any rectangle, rhombus and square? Why?

mark_scheme.text:
(1) The midpoint quadrilateral of any quadrilateral is a parallelogram. Reason: Assume that the midpoints of each side of the quadrilateral ABCD are E, F, G, and H in order. In △ABC, EF∥AC; in △CDA, GH∥AC, so EF∥GH. In the same way, FG∥BD is in △BCD, and EH∥BD is in △DAB, so FG∥EH. The two sets of opposite sides are parallel, so EFGH is a parallelogram (Varignon's theorem).
(2) The midpoint quadrilateral of any parallelogram is still a parallelogram. The reason is the same as (1); and each side is parallel to the two diagonals of the original parallelogram, and the side lengths are equal to half of the corresponding diagonals.
(3) The midpoint quadrilateral of a rectangle is a rhombus; the midpoint quadrilateral of a rhombus is a rectangle; the midpoint quadrilateral of a square is a square. Reason: The adjacent sides of the midpoint quadrilateral are parallel to the two diagonals of the original figure, and the side lengths are half of the two diagonals; the diagonals of the rectangle are equal ⇒ the adjacent sides of the midpoint quadrilateral are equal ⇒ it is a rhombus; the diagonals of the rhombus are perpendicular to each other ⇒ the adjacent sides of the midpoint quadrilateral are perpendicular to each other ⇒ it is a rectangle; the diagonals of the square are both equal and perpendicular to each other ⇒ the midpoint quadrilateral is both a rhombus and a rectangle ⇒ it is a square.

examiner_comment.text: Core conclusion: The quadrilateral obtained by connecting the midpoints of each side of a quadrilateral is a parallelogram (Varignon's theorem). Prove using the midpoint line of a triangle: EF∥AC in △ABC, GH∥AC in △CDA, so EF∥GH; similarly FG∥EH, so the midpoint quadrilateral is a parallelogram. Further: its sides are parallel to the two diagonals of the original quadrilateral, and the side lengths are equal to half of the corresponding diagonals. Therefore, they are classified according to the diagonal properties of the original figure: a rectangle with equal diagonals ⇒ a midpoint quadrilateral with four equal sides is a rhombus; a rhombus with vertical diagonals ⇒ a midpoint quadrilateral with right angles is a rectangle; a square with equal and vertical diagonals ⇒ a midpoint quadrilateral with both rhombus and rectangular properties is a square.

stem: What quadrilateral can be formed from two congruent triangles cut out of cardboard? What two congruent triangles are needed to form a rectangle? How about forming a rhombus or a square? Cut it out and explain why.
stem_lead: What quadrilateral can be formed from two congruent triangles cut out of cardboard? What two congruent triangles are needed to form a rectangle? How about forming a rhombus or a square? Cut it out and explain why.

mark_scheme.text: Two congruent triangles can be assembled into a parallelogram (just overlap and join one of the corresponding sides of the two triangles). To form a rectangle, you need two congruent right triangles (joined along the hypotenuse, which forms the diagonal of the rectangle). To form a rhombus, two congruent isosceles triangles are needed (joined together along the base, and the base is a diagonal of the rhombus). To form a square, two congruent isosceles right triangles are required (satisfying the conditions of both rectangle and rhombus).

examiner_comment.text: Use the reverse thinking of "a quadrilateral can be divided into two congruent triangles along the diagonal": a parallelogram can be divided into two congruent triangles along a diagonal, so the two congruent triangles can be combined into a parallelogram along the corresponding sides; a rectangle can be formed into two congruent right triangles along the diagonal, so to form a rectangle, two congruent right triangles must be combined along the Join the hypotenuse; the rhombus is divided into two congruent triangles along the diagonal and the two waists are adjacent (equal) sides of the rhombus, so each triangle is an isosceles triangle, and can be formed into a rhombus by joining along the base; a square is both a rectangle and a rhombus, and the diagonal is divided into two congruent isosceles right triangles, so a square can be formed by using two congruent isosceles right triangles.

stem: Prove: The sum of the squares of the two diagonals of a parallelogram is equal to the sum of the squares of the four sides.
stem_lead: Prove: The sum of the squares of the two diagonals of a parallelogram is equal to the sum of the squares of the four sides.

mark_scheme.text: Assume that in parallelogram ABCD, AB=a, BC=b, and the two diagonals are AC and BD, then: AC^2+BD^2=2(a^2+b^2)=AB^2+BC^2+CD^2+DA^2.

examiner_comment.text: Let ∠ABC=θ. According to the cosine theorem, in △ABC: AC^2=a^2+b^2-2abcosθ; in △ABD, ∠BAD=180°-θ, and AD=BC=b, there is BD^2=a^2+b^2-2abcos(180°-θ)=a^2+b^2+2abcosθ. Adding the two equations gives AC^2+BD^2=2(a^2+b^2). And the opposite sides of the parallelogram are equal: AB=CD=a, BC=AD=b, so AB^2+BC^2+CD^2+DA^2=a^2+b^2+a^2+b^2=2(a^2+b^2). Therefore AC^2+BD^2=AB^2+BC^2+CD^2+DA^2.

examiner_comment.text: Let the angle between the diagonal and the horizontal side be α (0°<α<90°). The two diagonals are symmetrical about the horizontal, and the acute angle they form is min(2α, 180°−2α). The problem is that there is a set of diagonal angles of 50°, that is, the acute angle between the two diagonals is 50°, so min(2α, 180°−2α)=50°. The solution is α=25° or α=65°, the corresponding diagonal angle with one set of sides is 25°, and the angle with the other set of sides is 90°−25°=65° (or vice versa). Therefore the angles formed by the diagonal and the sides are 25° and 65°.

(4) There is $10\mathrm{L}$ of water in the pool, and there will be water leakage of $0.05\mathrm{L}$ per hour thereafter. The amount of water $V$ (unit: L) in the pool changes with the change of time $t$ (unit: h).
stem_lead:
Which quantities are independent variables in the following questions? Which quantities are functions of independent variables? Try to write the analytical expression of the function.

(1) Changing the side length $x$ of the square, the area $S$ of the square changes accordingly.
(2) Water is injected into a pool $0.1\mathrm{m}^3$ every minute, and the water injection amount $y$ (unit: $\mathrm{m}^3$) changes with the change of water injection time $x$ (unit: min).
(3) The cultivated land area of Xiushui Village is $10^{6}\mathrm{m}^{2}$. The per capita cultivated land area of this village $y$ (unit: $\mathrm{m}^2$) changes with the change of the number of people in the village $n$.
(4) There is $10\mathrm{L}$ of water in the pool, and there will be water leakage of $0.05\mathrm{L}$ per hour thereafter. The amount of water $V$ (unit: L) in the pool changes with the change of time $t$ (unit: h).

mark_scheme.text:
(1) Independent variable: side length x; function: area S; analytical formula: S=x^2.
(2) Independent variable: time x (min); function: water injection amount y (m^3); analytical formula: y=0.1x.
(3) Independent variable: number of people n; function: per capita cultivated land area y (m^2); analytical formula: y=10^6/n.
(4) Independent variable: time t (h); function: water volume V (L); analytical formula: V=10-0.05t (valid when t≥0 and V≥0).

examiner_comment.text:
(1) The area of ​​a square is equal to the square of the side length. Changes in the side length cause the area to change, so x is the independent variable and S is the function: S=x^2.
(2) Inject 0.1m^3 per minute, and the total amount injected in x minutes is 0.1×x, so x is the independent variable, y=0.1x.
(3) The total cultivated land area is fixed at 10^6m^2, and the per capita area = total area ÷ number of people. Changes in the number of people n cause y to change, so y=10^6/n.
(4) The initial water volume is 10L, and the leakage is 0.05L per hour. After t hours, it is reduced by 0.05t, so V=10-0.05t (usually t ≥ 0 and no leakage becomes a negative number).

stem_lead:
Is $y$ in the following equation a function of $x$? Why?

(1) $y = 3x - 5$

(2) $y = \frac{x - 2}{x - 1}$

(3) $y = \sqrt{x - 1}$

Please give some more examples of functions

mark_scheme.text:
(1) is a function. For any real number x, there is a unique corresponding y=3x-5.
(2) is a function (in the range of x≠1). It is meaningless for the denominator to be 0 when x=1; for every x≠1, there is a unique y=(x-2)/(x-1).
(3) is a function (in the range of x≥1). The root requires x-1≥0; for every x≥1, there is a unique non-negative y=√(x-1).
Function examples: y=2x+1; y=x^2; y=|x|; y=1/x (x≠0); y=sin x.

examiner_comment.text:
The criterion for judging "whether y is a function of x": Within a given value range of x, each x can only correspond to one and only y.
(1) A linear expression can calculate a unique y for any x, so it is a function whose domain is all real numbers.
(2) The denominator of the fraction cannot be 0, so the domain is x≠1; in this domain, each x is substituted to obtain a unique y, so it is a function.
(3) The square root requires the radicand ≥ 0, that is, x-1 ≥ 0 → x ≥ 1; in this domain, each x corresponds to a unique (principal value) square root y, so it is a function.

examiner_comment.text: From each vertex of the n-sided polygon, it can be connected to (n-3) vertices other than itself and the two adjacent vertices to form a diagonal line. However, each diagonal is counted once by its two endpoints and needs to be divided by 2 to obtain the total number of diagonals f(n)=n(n-3)/2. Substitute n=5 to get 5; n=6 to get 9.

examiner_comment.text:
The general form of a linear function is y=kx+b(k≠0), and the proportional function is y=kx(k≠0, and b=0).
(1) y=-8x, consistent with y=kx (and k=-8≠0), so it is both a linear function and a proportional function.
(2) y=-8/x, including 1/x, is not in the form of y=kx+b, so it is not a linear function or a proportional function.
(3) y=5x^2+6, including x^2, is a quadratic function, not a linear function, nor a proportional function.
(4) y=-0.5x-1, consistent with y=kx+b (k=-0.5≠0), is a linear function; but b=-1≠0, so it is not a proportional function.

Determine the available intercept and slope of a straight line passing through a quadrant: look at the intersection position with the coordinate axis and combine it with the direction of the slope.

stem: In order to encourage students to participate in physical exercise, the school decided to purchase a batch of sports shoes for students to choose from. Please design a survey plan with a sample size of 30, calculate the mean, mode, and median of the sample, and make suggestions for the school to purchase sports shoes.
stem_lead: In order to encourage students to participate in physical exercise, the school decided to purchase a batch of sports shoes for students to choose from. Please design a survey plan with a sample size of 30, calculate the mean, mode, and median of the sample, and make suggestions for the school to purchase sports shoes.

mark_scheme.text:
[Survey plan (sample size 30)]
1) Survey target: all students in the school.
2) Sampling method: stratified random sampling. Stratified according to "grade (such as seventh/eighth/ninth grade) × gender (male/female)", 5 people are randomly selected from each layer, a total of 3×2×5=30 people.
3) Survey content (questionnaire/interview): Record the price (rupees) of sports shoes acceptable to each student (size, style preference, etc. can also be recorded at the same time).
4) Data sorting: Summarize and sort the "acceptable prices" of 30 people, and calculate the average, mode, and median.

[Sample data example (acceptable price for 30 people, unit: rupees)]
180, 200, 200, 220, 220, 220, 230, 240, 240, 240, 250, 250, 250, 260, 260, 260, 260, 270, 270, 280, 280, 280, 290, 300, 300, 300, 320, 330, 350, 360.

【Statistics】
Average: 7910÷30≈263.7 (rupees)
Mode: 260 (rupees) (appears 4 times)
Median: The 15th and 16th data are both 260, so the median = 260 (rupees)

【Purchase advice】
It is recommended that schools use the mid-range price range of about 260 rupees as the main purchasing range (for example, 240 to 300 rupees), and appropriately configure a small amount of lower-priced and higher-priced styles to cover different needs.

examiner_comment.text: Stratified random sampling ensures that all grades and genders are represented; after sorting the sample data: mean = sum/30; the mode is the data that appears most frequently; the median is an even number because n=30, so the average of the 15th and 16th data is taken. The 15th and 16th items in this sample are both 260, so the median is 260, and the mode is also 260, indicating that the mainstream accepted price is concentrated around 260 yuan, and a purchasing range recommendation is proposed accordingly.

stem: Calculate the time spent by the whole class in school, organize, describe and analyze the data to see what conclusions you can draw.
stem_lead: Calculate the time spent by the whole class in school, organize, describe and analyze the data to see what conclusions you can draw.

mark_scheme.text:
Reference conclusion (example):
1) Group the class’s school time data into intervals (such as 0–10, 10–20, 20–30, 30–40, 40 and above), make a frequency (frequency) table and draw a bar chart/histogram.
2) Calculate and describe central tendency: mean, central value, mode (the most concentrated interval).
3) Calculate and describe the degree of dispersion: range (maximum value − minimum value). If necessary, compare the proportion of people in each interval.
4) Conclusion example: Most students spend a certain time in school (such as 10-20 minutes), and the average/median time is about a certain value; a few students spend significantly longer time (may be outliers), and it is necessary to pay attention to the reasons such as distance, transportation mode, or travel time.
5) Examples of suggestions: For students who take a long time, you can consider adjusting the departure time, optimizing routes or transportation methods. The school can combine data to optimize school bus/school arrival management.

examiner_comment.text: Problem-solving ideas: This is a statistical practice question with no unique numerical answer. Complete the process of "collecting data→organizing (grouping, tables)→describing (charts, average/median/mode)→analyzing (concentration intervals, outliers, reasons and suggestions)". The conclusion needs to correspond to the actual statistical results and be supported by data or charts.
